plain_language.what_did_we_find: Provisional: source review shows that the operating-system memory high-water reported when a child exits can include descendants whose usage was accounted to that child. The earlier statement that descendants are excluded is too strong. No selected terms or checker measurements exist.
plain_language.is_it_interesting: Yes, because memory labels must describe what the operating system actually reports. The measurement remains useful but is not guaranteed to be exclusive memory of one executable or simultaneous memory of a whole process group.
plain_language.does_it_require_more_work: Correct the candidate protocol and final report labels before freeze, preserve this correction with the staged review, and keep direct process identity plus sampled group memory as separately qualified observations.

superseded_statement: OS child lifetime high-water includes startup/exit, uses bound host units and excludes descendant memory
corrected_statement: The wait4-reported child accounting high-water includes startup/exit and may include accounted-for descendants. It is neither a guaranteed exclusive executable peak nor a simultaneous process-group peak. Preserve the raw ru_maxrss value, host units and exact direct target identity.

source_findings.locations: proc_exit final-rusage assembly around lines 2297–2305; wait4 copyout around lines 2750–2761
source_findings.finding: The final child usage is combined with accumulated child-descendant usage before wait4 returns it.
The combination takes the larger ru_maxrss rather than adding simultaneous memory.

source_scope: Read-only inspection of Apple-published XNU main source on the recorded date; this is a conservative attribution caveat, not proof that this exact running kernel equals that source revision.
